fullPassage: We all understand differently — this much is obvious. The reason we understand differently is that our memories are different. Our experiences simply are not yours. In order to understand anything, we must find the closest item in memory to which it relates. Schank and Abelson claimed that understanding required one to find the correct knowledge structure, and to use that structure to create expectations for what events were likely to take place, so that new events could be understood in terms of what was normal. Thus, when a story about a cocktail party was being told, an understander brought out his cocktail party script which told him about what ordinarily happens at cocktail parties, and he used that script to guide his understanding of the story he was about to hear.

questions.passage: Schank and Abelson claimed that understanding __________ (require) one to find the correct knowledge structure.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: require(요구하다) → required(과거형: 요구했다)
det.analysis: that절 내에서 주절 동사 claimed(과거)에 시제 일치. require → required(과거형). 'understanding required one to find' = 이해는 ~을 찾도록 요구했다
det.tip: 시제 일치: 주절 claimed(과거) → that절도 과거 required

questions.passage: We must find the closest item in memory to which it __________. (relate)
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: relate(관련시키다) → relates(3인칭 단수 현재형)
det.analysis: 주어 it(3인칭 단수) + 현재시제(일반적 진술). relate → relates. 'to which it relates' = 그것이 관련되는 대상
det.tip: 관계대명사절 내 주어 it → 3인칭 단수 현재 relates

questions.passage: We all understand differently — this much is obvious. The reason we understand differently is that our memories are different. Our experiences simply are not yours. In order to understand anything, we must find the closest item in memory to which it relates. Schank and Abelson claimed that understanding required one to find the correct knowledge structure, and to use that structure to create expectations for what events were likely to __________, so that new events could be understood in terms of what was normal. Thus, when a story about a cocktail party was being told, an understander brought out his cocktail party script which told him about what ordinarily happens at cocktail parties, and he used that script to guide his understanding of the story he was about to hear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 어떤 사건이 발생할 가능성이 있는지에 대한 기대를 만들다
det.analysis:
✅ ① take place(발생하다): 어떤 사건이 발생할 가능성에 대한 기대 — 원문 일치 ←정답
❌ ② break down(고장나다/무너지다): 사건이 고장난다는 것은 문맥 부적절
❌ ③ stand out(눈에 띄다): 사건이 눈에 띈다는 것은 기대 생성과 무관
❌ ④ carry on(계속하다): 사건이 계속된다는 것은 발생 여부와 다른 의미

questions.passage: We all understand differently — this much is obvious. The reason we understand differently is that our memories are different. Our experiences simply are not yours. In order to understand anything, we must find the closest item in memory to which it relates. Schank and Abelson claimed that understanding required one to find the correct knowledge structure, and to use that structure to create expectations for what events were likely to take place, so that new events could be understood __________ what was normal. Thus, when a story about a cocktail party was being told, an understander brought out his cocktail party script which told him about what ordinarily happens at cocktail parties, and he used that script to guide his understanding of the story he was about to hear.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 정상적인 것의 관점에서 새 사건을 이해하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① in spite of(~에도 불구하고): 양보의 의미로 문맥 부적절
❌ ② in search of(~을 찾아서): 찾는 행위이지 관점이 아님
❌ ③ on behalf of(~을 대신하여): 대리의 의미로 문맥 부적절
✅ ④ in terms of(~의 관점에서): 정상적인 것의 관점에서 새 사건 이해 — 원문 일치 ←정답
det.tip: in terms of = ~의 관점에서, ~에 의하면 (from the perspective of)
